The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: not wanting to work.

notes: In everyday Mexican Spanish, 'flojo' is much more common than 'perezoso' to mean lazy.
As a masculine noun ('el perezoso'), it also means the tree-dwelling animal 'sloth'.

senses.definition: Of a person: unwilling to work or make an effort.

examples.text: Es muy perezoso y nunca quiere ayudar con los quehaceres.
examples.translation: He is very lazy and never wants to help with the chores.

notes: While 'perezoso' refers to a person who avoids work or effort, you might also hear 'flojo' in Mexico. 'Flojo' is very common in everyday conversation to describe someone who is lazy or lacks motivation.

senses.definition: Not wanting to work or make any physical effort.

examples.text: Es muy perezoso y nunca quiere ayudar con los deberes.
examples.translation: He is very lazy and never wants to help with the chores.
examples.emotion: annoyed and tired of dealing with someone who won't help

senses.definition: A mammal known for moving extremely slowly and living in trees.

examples.text: El perezoso vive en los árboles de la selva.
examples.translation: The sloth lives in the trees of the jungle.
examples.emotion: calm and observational, describing an interesting creature
